### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, touching **77** documentable anchor(s).

**37** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9dc1f42d50b2ee0c0afe8b6b7d7922b7c912f83a`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `logError (6 routes)`, `packageId (4 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 37 pages)`
- **23** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9dc1f42d50b2ee0c0afe8b6b7d7922b7c912f83a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d0f22d3740a5c4d14580cc95ddaeda3475bcb5a6` — the merge of head `4aa031c97c228fa7aa8b8a61c5e333cc051416f6` into base `9dc1f42d50b2ee0c0afe8b6b7d7922b7c912f83a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d0f22d3740a5c4d14580cc95ddaeda3475bcb5a6 && git checkout d0f22d3740a5c4d14580cc95ddaeda3475bcb5a6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9dc1f42d50b2ee0c0afe8b6b7d7922b7c912f83a 4aa031c97c228fa7aa8b8a61c5e333cc051416f6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9dc1f42d50b2ee0c0afe8b6b7d7922b7c912f83a && git merge --no-ff 4aa031c97c228fa7aa8b8a61c5e333cc051416f6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9dc1f42d50b2ee0c0afe8b6b7d7922b7c912f83a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9dc1f42d50b2ee0c0afe8b6b7d7922b7c912f83a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `4aa031c97c228fa7aa8b8a61c5e333cc051416f6`
Local-runs: none

Seat read on the declaration face. The PR declares `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, which is the face this tier serves, with no narrowing, no published schema and no governed path. The read covers the net diff against `main` (6 files, +1,567 / −0), the measurement 6353200007, the seat's GO 6353222762 and option A 6353787407, the os-dev-report 6354303990, and the check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **It refuses nothing and writes no row of its own: right.** `reportAccessUpgrade` runs at `kernel:bootstrapped`, beside `catalog-reference-report.ts`. The only write is the `single` notification through `messaging.emit()`. `security-plugin.ts` wraps the call, so a failed report logs a warning and never fails the boot.
2. **Fail-closed reads: right.**
   - `scanAll` (the activation ledger, `sys_sharing_rule`) throws `ReportStop` on any read fault, and so does the catalog list or `listDeclaredRules`. A stopped report says what it could not read and delivers nothing.
   - An object the composition does not register is listed under `absent`, not guessed.
3. **Findings match the GO: right.**
   - orphans;
   - suspected re-enablements: a ledger row's `package_id` against the entry's `packageId`, with candidates and, for a permission set, the positions binding it;
   - sharing-rule collisions per organization;
   - broken references in customer items;
   - field denies a same-object customer set lacks.
   The two accepted limits are stated: candidates, and "same object" rather than "copied from".
4. **Delivery: right.**
   - `single`: the Default Organization's `admin_full_access` holders plus `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`, stamped with the Default Organization.
   - Walled: no emit, and one `error` line addressed to the operator (option A).
   - `dedupKey` is the finding set's digest, so an unchanged set notifies once; the dev measured this across two `single` boots.
   - Each non-delivery (no messaging service, no recipient, an unreadable audience, a refused emit) is logged with its own cause and fix.
5. **New public surface: one member.** `SharingRuleService.listDeclaredRules()` on plugin-sharing's exported class. It reads only, and returns `null` when the service reads no declarations. The report's own exports are not re-exported from plugin-security's index.
6. **Observations, not blocking:**
   - the report runs at every boot, not only after a package change, because no version is recorded to detect one; the digest makes the repeat silent;
   - both tables are read whole, which is bounded by the customer's ledger and rule counts;
   - the walled line echoes the configured operator address or addresses into the server log.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/plugin-security` and `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` at `patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **`yes (widening)` is right**, and it is the value both carriers now read: the changeset at this head, and the PR body as amended by the seat. The widening is the new public `listDeclaredRules()`. The notification topic is a free-form string on an existing ingress, not a published key.
- **`patch` is right** under the house rule: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and no authorable key moves.
- `Check Changeset` is success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The walled channel** is ruled A (6353787407). Option C, an organization-less operator notification, is put to the maintainer as a card of its own and does not block this PR.
- **Mandatory topic:** not set. A recipient's mute can hide it, and the changeset names the existing `mandatoryTopics` operator option that makes it mute-proof. Accepted.
- **Out-of-scope observation:** no example app declares `@objectstack/organizations`, so a walled `os serve` of a shipped example refuses at boot. Carried by the seat; not this PR's.
- **R1–R4** were measured by the dev on the final head (see the ACCEPT).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24446-u1-access-upgrade-comparison`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Y5583bs2RDd53MH6kM1ca3`

**VERDICT: PASS**

Seat ACCEPT · epic PM `session_01Y5583bs2RDd53MH6kM1ca3` (`os-steve`) · 2026-10-23T01:00Z. PR #25311 at `4aa031c97c228fa7aa8b8a61c5e333cc051416f6` (#24446 U1; claim 6353092498; measurement 6353200007; GO 6353222762; walled option A 6353787407; report 6354303990). **ACCEPT.**

## Seat check

- **Shape:** 6 files, +1,567 / −0:
  - plugin-security's new `access-upgrade-report.ts`, its unit and wiring pins, and the boot wiring in `security-plugin.ts`;
  - plugin-sharing's new public `SharingRuleService.listDeclaredRules()`;
  - one changeset.
  `check-governed-merges --pr 25311`: not governed, so this is an ordinary queue landing. It touches no ceremony, plan, harness or tenancy read, so no `needs:upgrade-harness`; the dev ran the harness locally.
- **Review tier:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, so the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Seat record 6354822120 on this head: PASS.
  - The value was first declared `no`. The seat corrected it, because the widening is the new public member on an exported class: the dev fixed the changeset in `c945716b7`, and the seat amended the PR body.
- **What it does** (ruling 6259332195 items 1–2, the access class; ADR-0126 §6 wall 3): at `kernel:bootstrapped`, it compares the customer's access state with the registry this boot holds. It covers the activation ledger for positions, permission sets and sharing rules; customer-authored permission sets; and `sys_sharing_rule` rows. It reports:
  - orphans;
  - suspected re-enablements;
  - sharing-rule collisions;
  - broken references;
  - uncovered field denies.
  It writes and refuses nothing.
- **Delivery:**
  - `single`: one deduplicated `messaging.emit()` notification to the Default Organization's administrators and the configured operator.
  - Walled: one `error` line addressed to the operator (option A), with no emit.
  - Every non-delivery is logged with its cause.
- **CI on the head:** 41 check-runs, every one success or skipped, including `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Check Changeset`. The unlabelled harness lane is skipped. Mergeable clean.
- **R1–R4,** measured by the dev on this head, after the main merge:
  - Build, plugin-security (4,442 passed) and plugin-sharing (1,201 passed); typecheck 0.
  - R1: a fresh boot logs a clean report, with nothing absent.
  - R4: a production `os serve` on a persistent database, clean boot, then CONTROL, then a vendor rename.
    - `isolated` and `group`: the CONTROL reports nothing. After the rename: 1 re-enablement and 1 operator line, 0 refused writes, 0 "reached no administrator", 0 `sys_notification` rows.
    - `single`: 1 re-enablement, and exactly 1 notification, which is deduplicated on the next boot.
  - R2 and R3: the harness passed 16/16, both fixture legs, measured on `68e1310b7`, which carries the same source.
- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/plugin-security` and `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` at `patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Right under the house rule. The two accepted limits (ADR-0126 §9) and the `mandatoryTopics` option are stated.
- **Carried, not this PR's:**
  - option C (an in-app operator notification under a wall) is with the maintainer;
  - no example app declares `@objectstack/organizations`, so a walled R4 needs a temporary edit. That is with the maintainer as a possible p3 card.
- **Landing:** the seat flips the PR ready and enables auto-merge. `Part of #24446`: the card stays open for U2 and the ADR-0126 note.
